q.t: Objects that give out their own light are called…
q.e: Luminous objects emit light — the Sun, stars, fire, fireflies, lamps.

q.t: Is the Moon luminous?
o: Yes — it makes its own light
q.e: Moonlight is reflected sunlight.

q.t: Light travels in…
q.e: Experiments with aligned holes and bent pipes show light goes straight.

q.t: Glass that lets almost all light pass is…
q.e: Transparent materials let light through almost completely.

q.t: Tracing paper lets some light through. It is…
q.e: Translucent materials let light pass partially.

q.t: Cardboard blocks light completely. It is…
q.e: Opaque objects let no light through and cast the darkest shadows.

q.t: A shadow is…
o: A dark patch where light does not reach
q.e: An object blocks light, leaving a dark area behind it.

q.t: The bouncing back of light from a shiny surface is…
q.e: Reflection changes the direction of light at a shiny surface.

q.t: The image in a pinhole camera is…
q.e: Rays cross at the pinhole, so the image is inverted.

q.t: A periscope uses how many plane mirrors?
q.e: Two mirrors in a Z-shaped box let you see objects not directly in view.

q.t: What three things are needed to see a shadow?
o: A light source, an object, and a screen
A mirror, a lens and light
q.e: Light must be blocked by an object, and the shadow must fall on a screen (wall, ground).

q.t: A red ball and a blue ball of the same size cast shadows. The shadows are…
q.e: A shadow is the absence of light, so it has no colour of its own.

q.t: Moving an object closer to the light source makes its shadow…
q.e: The object blocks a wider cone of light, so the shadow grows.

q.t: In a plane mirror, the image is…
q.e: A plane mirror image is erect, same size, laterally inverted, and can't be caught on a screen.

q.t: You raise your left hand in front of a mirror. Your image raises its…
q.e: Plane mirrors swap left and right — lateral inversion.

q.t: Why is 'AMBULANCE' painted reversed on ambulances?
o: So it reads correctly in a rear-view mirror
q.e: The mirror's lateral inversion flips it back to normal for the driver ahead.

q.t: In the three-matchbox experiment, moving one box sideways makes the light spot…
q.e: The holes are no longer in a straight line, and light can't bend to get through.

q.t: A candle is visible through a straight pipe but not a bent one. This shows…
q.e: If light could curve, you'd see the candle through the bent pipe too.

q.t: A kaleidoscope uses mirrors arranged in a…
q.e: Three mirror strips in a triangle make reflections of reflections.

q.t: Why must LED lamps be disposed of properly?
o: They should be recycled, not thrown in garbage
q.e: At end of life, LED lamps should go for proper disposal or recycling.

q.t: Why is a pinhole camera image upside down?
o: Light from top goes down through the hole, and from bottom goes up
q.e: Light travels in straight lines, so rays from the top and bottom cross at the pinhole and swap places.

q.t: Can a plane mirror image be obtained on a screen?
o: Only if the mirror is large
q.e: The image only appears to be behind the mirror; no light actually meets there.

q.t: You stand 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is your image behind the mirror (m)?
q.e: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

q.t: In the last question, how far are you from your image (m)?
q.e: 2 m to the mirror + 2 m behind it = 4 m.

q.t: A translucent object casts a shadow that is…
q.e: Some light still passes through, so the shadow is lighter.

q.t: Which pair is matched correctly?
o: Mirror image — laterally inverted; pinhole image — upside down
Mirror image — upside down; pinhole — erect
q.e: Different causes: reflection swaps left–right; crossing rays at the pinhole flip top–bottom.

q.t: Where is a periscope useful?
q.e: Two mirrors let you see objects not directly visible, like above water from a submarine.

q.t: The shadow of an object can change shape when you…
q.e: The shape depends on the object's outline as seen from the light — tilting changes that outline.

q.t: Why can you see a book that doesn't make its own light?
o: It reflects light into your eyes
q.e: Non-luminous objects are seen by the light they reflect.

q.t: Which is non-luminous?
q.e: The Moon only reflects sunlight.

q.t: An object moves from near the light towards the screen. Its shadow becomes…
q.e: Closer to the screen, the object blocks less of the spreading light, so the shadow is smaller and sharper.

q.t: The word 'MOM' seen in a plane mirror reads…
q.e: M and O are symmetric left-to-right, and the word is a palindrome, so lateral inversion leaves it unchanged.

q.t: A pinhole camera is pointed at a tree. The image on the screen shows the tree…
q.e: The image is inverted and shows the colours of the object.

q.t: Why does a shadow reveal only the outline of an object?
o: It is just the area where light is blocked
q.e: Light either reaches a place or not; the shadow shows the blocked area only.

q.t: Which Indian art form uses shadows?
q.e: Shadow puppetry places cut-out puppets between a lamp and a screen.

q.t: What is the Aranmula Kannadi?
o: A traditional metal mirror from Kerala
q.e: It is a polished metal-surface mirror, made for centuries before glass mirrors.

q.t: Why does the kaleidoscope show a new pattern every turn?
o: Reflections of reflections of moving bangle pieces
q.e: Moving the pieces changes every reflected copy, forming a new pattern.

q.t: A student says a shadow has the colour of the object. Which observation disproves this?
o: A red and a green ball both cast dark shadows
Shadows are bigger near the light
q.e: Different-coloured objects give the same dark shadow.

q.t: Using a mirror, a sunlit spot is thrown onto a dark wall. Tilting the mirror…
q.e: Light still travels straight; the mirror sends it in a new direction as you tilt it.

q.t: Why should you never point a laser at someone's eyes?
o: It can seriously damage the eyes
q.e: A concentrated beam can injure the eye.
